context_requirements: Active PKC-dependent signaling (e.g., GNAQ/GNA11 mutation, BCR signaling, or high PKC expression)
Proliferative or survival signaling dependent on PKC effectors such as MAPK, AKT, or NF-kB
Prolonged drug exposure sufficient to downregulate PKC (effects are typically delayed beyond 6 h)
falsifiers: No decrease in proliferation or cell-cycle genes at 24 h in any line
No change in MAPK-dependent immediate-early genes (FOS, JUN, EGR1, DUSP6) at 6 h
Strong and uniform transcriptional response across all nine lines, including HA1E
Predominant upregulation of proliferation genes rather than downregulation

evidence.supports: Prolonged PKC inhibition downregulates PKC and inhibits proliferation, induces differentiation, and promotes apoptosis in tumor cell lines.
PKC inhibitor AEB071 attenuates BCR survival signaling and decreases c-Myc, Cyclin D1, and CD44 expression.
PKC inhibitors suppress MAPK signaling in GNAQ/GNA11-mutant uveal melanoma, but PI3K/AKT remains active and limits sensitivity.
Enzastaurin combined with immunotoxin causes loss of Mcl-1 and AKT and activates caspase 3/7, but PKC inhibition alone is insufficient.
